title: Meter Services Standard — Estimated-Read Limits and High-Bill Re-Read Threshold for the Utility Pass-Through Service
content:
These figures govern estimated reads and verification re-reads of submeters on the Utility Pass-Through Service. They apply on the submetered schedules only; the Flat-Rate Water, Sewer & Trash Schedule has no meter reads.

## Figures by schedule

| Service schedule | Most consecutive billing periods on an estimated read | Actual-read periods averaged for an estimate | High-bill re-read threshold (percent of baseline consumption) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flat-Rate Water, Sewer & Trash Schedule | not applicable | not applicable | not applicable |
| Submetered Water Schedule | 2 | 3 | 150 |
| Submetered Water & Sewer Schedule | 2 | 3 | 150 |
| Submetered Water, Sewer & Natural Gas Schedule | 2 | 3 | 150 |
| Submetered Water, Sewer & Propane Schedule | 2 | 3 | 150 |
| Submetered Electric, Water & Sewer Schedule | 2 | 3 | 150 |

## What each figure means

- **Most consecutive billing periods on an estimated read**: the largest number of consecutive billing periods that may be billed on an estimated read before an actual read must be obtained.
- **Actual-read periods averaged for an estimate**: the number of most recent actual-read billing periods whose average daily consumption sets an estimated read.
- **High-bill re-read threshold**: consumption, as a percentage of the baseline, above which the meter is re-read before the statement is issued.

## Boundary reading of the limits

With a limit of 2 consecutive estimated periods, a third consecutive period may not be billed on an estimate. With a threshold of 150 percent, a consumption exactly at 150 percent of the baseline is not above the threshold; any consumption above 150 percent is.
